Decision-Trees: Reduced Error Pruning
Split training data into a growing and a pruning set
Learn a complete and consistent decision tree that classifies all examples in the growing set correctly
As long as the error on the pruning set does not increase, try to replace each node by a leaf, evaluate the resulting (sub-)tree on the pruning set then make the replacement the results in the maximum error reduction.

Decision-Trees: Decision Lists and Decision Graphs
Decision Lists
An ordered list of rules
The first rule that fires makes the prediction
can be learned with a covering approach
Decision Graphs
Similar to decision trees, but nodes may have multiple predecessors
Each decision tree can be converted into a rule set. A decision tree can be viewed as a set of non-overlapping rules and typically learned via divide-and-conquer algorithms (recursive partitioning) Transformation of rule sets / decision lists into trees is less trivial
Many concepts have a shorter description as a rule set
Low complexity decision lists are more expressive than low complexity decision trees
Exceptions: if one or more attributes are relevant for the classification of all examples

Regression Task: the target variable is numerical instead of discrete. Two principal approaches
Discretize the numerical target variable
Adapt the classification algorithm to regression data
Decision-Trees: Regression Trees
Differences to Decision Trees (Classification Trees)
Leaf Nodes: Predict the average value of all instances in this leaf
Splitting criterion: Minimize the variance of the values in each subset
Termination criteria: Lower bound on standard deviation in a node and lower bound on number of examples in a node
Pruning criterion: Numeric error measures, e.g. Mean-Squared Error

tree.name: Subtree replacement
tree.content: Subtree replacement removes a node from a decision tree and redistributes the instances of its leaf children to another node.

details.content: Subtree replacement is performed by deleting node B and moving instances of leaves 4 and 5 into node C.

tree.name: Subtree raising
tree.content: Subtree raising moves a subtree upward in a decision tree to replace a parent node, preserving classification while maintaining overall accuracy.

details.content: Subtree raising is an alternative to subtree replacement for pruning decision trees.

tree.name: Reduced error pruning
tree.content: Reduced error pruning uses a hold-out validation set to iteratively replace nodes with leaves while ensuring error does not increase.

details.content: The goal of reduced error pruning is to simplify the decision tree without increasing validation error.
Split training data into a growing set and a pruning set, learn a complete tree on the growing set, then evaluate replacements on the pruning set.
Reduced error pruning is essentially the same as pruning in rule learning.

tree.name: Decision list
tree.content: A decision list is an ordered list of rules where the first rule that fires determines the prediction for classification.

details.content: Decision lists can be learned with a covering approach.
Decision lists are used as an alternative representation to decision trees for classification.

tree.name: Decision graph
tree.content: A decision graph resembles a decision tree but permits nodes to have multiple predecessors, forming a directed acyclic graph structure.

details.content: Each decision tree can be converted into a rule set, and decision graphs can represent such rule sets with shared substructures.
Transforming rule sets or decision lists into decision graphs is less trivial than converting them into trees.

tree.name: Regression tree
tree.content: A regression tree predicts numeric values by assigning leaf nodes the average of target values and splitting to minimize variance.

details.content: In regression trees, leaf nodes predict the average value of all instances in the leaf.
The splitting criterion for regression trees is to minimize the variance of the target values in each subset.
Regression trees stop growing when the standard deviation in a node falls below a lower bound or the node contains fewer examples than a threshold.
Regression trees use numeric error measures such as mean-squared error for pruning.

tree.name: Regression task
tree.content: A regression task involves predicting a continuous numerical target variable instead of a discrete class label for supervised learning problems.

details.content: Regression tasks can be approached by discretizing the target variable or adapting classification algorithms to handle numeric outputs.
One principal approach to regression trees is to adapt the classification algorithm to regression data.

tree.name: Splitting criterion
tree.content: A splitting criterion determines how a decision tree node divides data, aiming to improve purity or reduce variance in subsets.

details.content: For regression trees, the splitting criterion minimizes the variance of the values in each subset.

tree.name: Termination criterion
tree.content: Termination criteria are conditions that stop splitting of a decision tree node, such as minimum standard deviation or instance count.

details.content: Regression trees use a lower bound on standard deviation in a node and a lower bound on number of examples as termination criteria.

tree.name: Pruning criterion
tree.content: A pruning criterion evaluates whether removing a subtree improves model performance, using numeric error measures like mean-squared error on validation.

details.content: Regression trees prune using numeric error measures, e.g., mean-squared error.
